summary: Coordinates LiveKit agent workers, job dispatch, worker registration, job lifecycle updates, and agent client RPC interactions. The package owns agent configuration, worker signal handling, job assignment and termination flows, and topic selection for agent namespaces and deployments.
responsibilities: Configure agent dispatch behavior and target load defaults.
Discover enabled agent workers and launch jobs through internal RPC topics.
Register workers, dispatch worker messages, and handle pings, availability, job updates, simulated jobs, and migration requests.
Track worker load, status, running jobs, availability responses, and job state transitions.

summary: Builds LiveKit client configuration overrides from static rules and Tengo-based client information match expressions. The package owns match expression compilation, client-info script objects, SDK/browser version comparison, static configuration items, and merged client configuration selection.
responsibilities: Compile and evaluate match rules against `livekit.ClientInfo`.
Expose client information fields to Tengo scripts.
Compare SDK and browser versions with semver fallback behavior.
Select, return, and merge static client configuration overrides.

summary: Defines LiveKit server configuration schema, defaults, YAML and CLI loading, API key validation, generated CLI flags, and logger initialization helpers.
responsibilities: Model server, RTC, room, TURN, API, logging, limits, metrics, tracing, node stats, and integration configuration.
Provide default values used as the base configuration for server startup.
Merge YAML configuration and CLI overrides into a validated Config.
Generate hidden or visible CLI flags from YAML-tagged config fields.
Validate API key configuration and initialize the global logger.

summary: Provides runtime metrics helpers for collecting RTT samples, merging metrics batches, normalizing timestamps, and periodically reporting metrics batches. The package owns the configuration defaults and worker loops used by these metric collection and reporting components.
responsibilities: Define metric collection, reporting, and timestamp normalization configuration.
Collect publisher, subscriber, and relay RTT samples into metrics batches.
Merge externally produced metrics batches and periodically emit non-empty batches.
Normalize metric timestamps using one-way delay estimation before downstream handling.

summary: The routing package defines the contracts and implementations used to coordinate LiveKit rooms, participant signal startup, node registration, and room-to-node placement. It provides local routing for single-node operation and Redis-backed routing for multi-node node discovery, room assignment, and keepalive-driven node health updates.
responsibilities: Define router, message sink/source, local node, signal client, and room manager client contracts.
Provide LocalRouter and RedisRouter implementations for single-node and distributed routing.
Persist and resolve room-to-node assignments for room creation and participant signal setup.
Track local node identity, region, lifecycle state, and resource statistics.
Relay participant signal streams through typed RPC streams and message channels.
Convert participant initialization state to and from LiveKit StartSession protos.

summary: Provides node selector implementations used to choose a LiveKit server node from candidate routing nodes. Selectors filter unavailable nodes, optionally prefer low-load or nearby-region nodes, and choose candidates using configured sorting and selection algorithms.
responsibilities: Define the NodeSelector contract and selector factory from server configuration.
Filter nodes by availability, serving state, CPU load, system load, and region proximity.
Select nodes using lowest-cost or power-of-two-choice algorithms.
Sort candidates by random, normalized system load, CPU load, rooms, clients, tracks, or bandwidth rate.
Expose selector errors and helper utilities for load and limit checks.

summary: The rtc package owns LiveKit room and local participant runtime behavior, including signaling, WebRTC transport coordination, media and data track publication, subscription management, migration, and room broadcasts. It connects protocol messages and participant state to SFU media forwarding, telemetry, routing, egress, and agent dispatch integrations.
responsibilities: Create and manage rooms, local participants, participant state, permissions, metadata, and lifecycle transitions.
Coordinate publisher and subscriber transports, SDP negotiation, ICE handling, reconnect, fallback, and migration behavior.
Publish media and data tracks, resolve subscriptions, dispatch RTP/RTCP and data messages, and maintain track metadata.
Broadcast participant, room, speaker, data, subscription, and signaling updates to clients and room listeners.
Enforce runtime limits and feature gates while reporting telemetry, metrics, connection quality, and egress failures.

summary: Owns data track packet header encoding and decoding, extension handling, and the participant SID extension used on data track packets. The package defines the wire layout helpers needed to marshal and unmarshal packet headers and payloads.
responsibilities: Encode and decode data track packet headers and payloads.
Track packet framing flags, sequence numbers, frame numbers, timestamps, and extension metadata.
Add, replace, find, marshal, and unmarshal packet extensions.
Represent the participant SID extension and validate its wire encoding.

summary: The dynacast package manages publisher-side subscription demand for audio codecs and video qualities. It aggregates local subscriber and downstream node interest, handles codec regression, debounces video downgrades, and notifies publishers when they should enable, disable, or reduce media layers.
responsibilities: Define dynacast manager, manager listener, quality listener, and per-codec quality tracker contracts.
Track audio codec enablement and video max subscribed quality per MIME type.
Aggregate subscriber and downstream node subscription demand into committed publisher notifications.
Handle codec regression by redirecting state from one codec quality tracker to another.
Queue listener notifications through a serialized operation queue.
Provide no-op manager, listener, and quality implementations for defaults and embedded unsupported operations.

summary: The signalling package defines participant signaling contracts and concrete helpers for handling client signal requests, writing asynchronous signal responses, and constructing LiveKit SignalResponse protobuf messages. It also provides no-op implementations used as embedded defaults or unsupported adapters.
responsibilities: Define participant signal handler, signaller, and outbound signaling interfaces.
Dispatch inbound SignalRequest messages to local participant operations.
Manage asynchronous response sinks and close or swap signal connections.
Build typed SignalResponse protobuf messages for room, participant, track, subscription, data track, and reconnection events.
Provide no-op signal handler, signaller, and signaling implementations.
Define sentinel signaling validation and permission errors.

summary: The supervisor package monitors local participant publication state and detects stalled publishing transitions. It coordinates per-track publication monitors, periodically checks them for timeout or recovery, and exposes callbacks for publication errors.
responsibilities: Track pending and active publications for a participant.
Forward participant peer connection, mute, published track, and cleared track events to per-publication monitors.
Periodically check publication monitors for timeout errors and idle state.
Report first publication errors through a callback and log later recovery.
Maintain per-track publication transition queues and timeout detection.

summary: The transport package defines callback contracts and negotiation state values for RTC transport integrations. It centralizes transport lifecycle, media, data, SDP, ICE, negotiation, stream-state, and unmatched-media callbacks along with default unimplemented behavior.
responsibilities: Define the transport Handler callback interface.
Provide sentinel errors for missing ICE, offer, and answer handlers.
Provide an UnimplementedHandler with no-op callbacks and default handler errors.
Represent negotiation state and convert it to stable string labels.

summary: The rtc/types package defines shared RTC contracts and value types used by participants, rooms, media tracks, data tracks, telemetry listeners, ICE tracking, protocol capability gates, and traffic accounting. It is an interface-heavy package that centralizes cross-package type boundaries without owning concrete RTC behavior.
responsibilities: Define participant, local participant, room, media track, data track, listener, resolver, and operation monitor contracts.
Represent participant migration state, participant close reasons, signaling close reasons, and protocol capability gates.
Track ICE connection candidates, selected candidate pairs, inferred connection type, and mDNS candidate detection.
Provide no-op participant and telemetry listener implementations.
Convert RTP stats snapshots into traffic counters, aggregate traffic counters, and compute traffic rates.

summary: The service package owns LiveKit server service-layer wiring and runtime APIs, including HTTP/Twirp endpoints, PSRPC services, room lifecycle management, RTC signalling, auth, persistence adapters, ingress, egress, SIP, agent, TURN, and WHIP operations. It coordinates configuration, routing, RTC runtime objects, telemetry, stores, and protocol RPC clients into the server process.
responsibilities: Construct and run the top-level LiveKit HTTP, Twirp, PSRPC, RTC, WHIP, agent, Prometheus, and TURN service surfaces.
Authorize API calls, validate room and participant requests, and map service failures to HTTP, Twirp, or PSRPC errors.
Manage rooms, participants, signalling sessions, room allocation, node selection, and local RTC room lifecycle.
Persist and query rooms, participants, egress, ingress, SIP, and agent state through local or Redis-backed stores.
Implement public service APIs for room, egress, ingress, SIP, agent dispatch, IO, RTC, WHIP, and signal relay workflows.

summary: Core SFU media forwarding package that connects upstream receivers to subscriber downtracks, translates RTP across negotiated codecs and layers, handles RTCP feedback, and reports media forwarding health.
responsibilities: Create and manage upstream receivers and subscriber downtracks.
Translate RTP sequence numbers, timestamps, payloads, header extensions, layers, RED, RTX, padding, and blank frames.
Allocate video layers based on bitrate, bandwidth, mute state, and stream availability.
Track RTP stats, forwarding latency, connection quality, playout delay, sender reports, and RTCP feedback.
Coordinate stream tracker events, receiver restarts, codec changes, and downtrack lifecycle transitions.

summary: Tracks per-participant audio activity level for SFU audio processing. The package converts RTP audio levels into smoothed linear activity values and reports whether recent audio should be considered active.
responsibilities: Define audio level activity, update interval, and smoothing configuration.
Observe audio levels by explicit duration or RTP timestamp progression.
Smooth observed audio levels and reset stale or completed observation windows.
Convert audio level decibel values into linear values.

summary: This package owns RTP and RTCP buffering for SFU media streams. It manages packet storage, RTP stats, NACK state, codec and layer metadata, dependency descriptor parsing, frame-rate calculation, video size tracking, RTX repair mapping, and buffer lifecycle callbacks.
responsibilities: Construct RTP buffers, RTCP readers, and SSRC-indexed buffer factories.
Bind RTP parameters, codecs, payload types, header extensions, stats, and packet buckets.
Process incoming RTP packets into extended packets with sequence adjustment, NACK state, bucket storage, video metadata, and read notifications.
Generate or expose RTCP-related state such as NACK pairs, reception reports, sender report data, and PLI requests.
Track video layers, frame integrity, frame rates, video sizes, audio levels, data byte stats, and stream restarts.

summary: This package defines the SFU bandwidth estimation contract and shared estimator state types. It provides enum values for estimator strategy and congestion state, plus interfaces for REMB, TWCC, RTT, probing, and congestion-state callbacks.
responsibilities: Define default RTT and RTT smoothing constants.
Represent bandwidth estimation strategy types.
Represent congestion states reported by bandwidth estimation implementations.
Declare the BWE interface for feedback handling, packet send tracking, probing, and state reporting.
Declare the listener interface for congestion state changes.

summary: This package implements remote bandwidth estimation for the SFU. It combines REMB estimates, expected bandwidth usage, repeated-NACK ratios, channel trend observation, probe control, RTT smoothing, and congestion-state callbacks.
responsibilities: Track remote estimate trends and repeated-NACK ratios for congestion detection.
Maintain remote BWE congestion state and committed channel capacity.
Control probe cluster lifecycle, hangover, finalization, and probe signals.
Process REMB feedback and notify listeners when congestion state changes.
Provide default configuration for channel observers, NACK tracking, probe control, and remote BWE behavior.

summary: Implements the send-side bandwidth estimator used by the SFU. The package tracks TWCC send and feedback data, groups packets into queuing measurements, evaluates loss and delay signals, manages probe clusters, and reports congestion state changes with an estimated available channel capacity.
responsibilities: Implement the `bwe.BWE` send-side estimator.
Track sent packets and consume transport-wide congestion control feedback.
Group acknowledged and lost packets into delay and loss measurements.
Detect early-warning and congested states from queuing delay, weighted loss, and captured traffic ratio trends.
Manage probe cluster lifecycle and probe-based capacity updates.

summary: Provides congestion-control helper utilities for probing available bandwidth and detecting trends in sampled values. The package owns probe cluster scheduling, probe regulation after congestion signals, probe signal enums, and generic trend detection based on sample windows.
responsibilities: Manage probe clusters that send padding probes at controlled rates and durations.
Regulate when probing can resume and how long probes should run after congestion signals.
Represent probe and trend state enums with stable string output.
Track numeric sample windows and infer upward, downward, or inconclusive trends.

summary: Provides codec-specific RTP payload header mungers used by the SFU forwarding path. The package defines the common codec munger contract, a no-op munger, and VP8 header rewriting logic for picture id, TL0 picture index, key index, padding, out-of-order packets, gaps, and temporal layer filtering.
responsibilities: Define the codec munger interface used by packet forwarding.
Provide a null munger for codecs or paths that do not need payload header rewriting.
Rewrite VP8 payload descriptors while preserving continuity across forwarding, layer switches, gaps, and padding.
Track VP8 picture id wrap-around and out-of-order picture id offsets.
Report codec-specific filtering and cache-miss errors.

summary: Calculates connection quality scores for SFU media streams from RTP delta statistics, receiver reports, packet loss, RTT, jitter, bitrate expectations, layer transitions, mute state, and pause state. The package also emits analytics stream statistics and maps internal scores to LiveKit connection quality and MOS values.
responsibilities: Collect RTP delta stats from receiver-side or sender-side providers.
Convert RTP stream and layer statistics into analytics payloads.
Score media quality from packet loss, RTT, jitter, bitrate, and layer distance.
Track mute, layer mute, pause, bitrate transition, and layer transition effects on scoring.
Map internal scores to MOS and `livekit.ConnectionQuality`.

summary: Provides data channel writing helpers for reliable and unreliable channels with bitrate-aware retry and drop behavior. The package also owns a sliding-window bitrate calculator used to estimate buffered throughput.
responsibilities: Calculate recent data channel bitrate over a sliding time window.
Wrap data channel write operations with deadlines.
Retry reliable writes when receivers are not considered slow.
Drop unreliable writes when buffered amount would exceed target latency.

summary: This package owns RTP interceptors that discover or repair simulcast and RTX stream identity metadata. It wraps remote RTP readers to inspect MID, RID, and repaired RID header extensions, report RTX repair/base SSRC pairs, and inject missing simulcast identity extensions for configured streams.
responsibilities: Create interceptor factories for RTX metadata extraction and unhandled simulcast repair.
Probe remote RTP streams for MID, RID, and repaired RID header extensions.
Match RTX repair streams with their base streams by MID and RID/RSID metadata.
Inject missing simulcast MID, RID, or repaired RID extensions when stream metadata is configured.
Preserve original readers when required header extensions or configured stream metadata are unavailable.

summary: Provides RTP packet pacing implementations for the SFU send path. The package defines pacer behavior types, packet containers, shared send logic, pass-through, no-queue, and leaky-bucket pacing strategies, and probe cluster observation for bandwidth probing.
responsibilities: Define the pacer interface and packet structure used by SFU forwarding.
Patch RTP abs-send-time and transport-wide congestion control extensions before sending.
Integrate packet sends with bandwidth estimation and probe observation.
Provide pass-through, wake-drained no-queue, and leaky-bucket pacing implementations.
Track probe cluster send progress and notify listeners when probe goals complete.

summary: Detects and sizes LKTS packet trailers at the end of RTP payloads. The package validates trailer eligibility using the RTP marker flag, a magic suffix, and an XORed trailer length byte.
responsibilities: Define the LKTS trailer magic suffix and trailer envelope constants.
Detect whether an RTP payload ends with an eligible packet trailer.
Return the number of bytes that should be stripped from packet payloads.

summary: Encodes, decodes, and rewrites the WebRTC absolute capture time RTP header extension. The package owns the extension URI, validation errors, NTP timestamp storage, optional capture clock offset handling, and binary wire serialization.
responsibilities: Define the absolute capture time RTP header extension URI.
Store absolute capture timestamps and optional estimated capture clock offsets.
Rewrite capture timestamps by a time offset.
Marshal and unmarshal shortened and extended absolute capture time payloads.

summary: Encodes and decodes the AV1 RTP dependency descriptor header extension. The package owns descriptor data models, bitstream readers and writers, dependency-structure parsing, template selection, and payload size calculation.
responsibilities: Represent dependency descriptors, frame dependency structures, templates, decode target indications, and render resolutions.
Read descriptor payloads from bit-packed RTP header extension bytes.
Write descriptor payloads using mandatory fields, extended fields, template structures, and frame-specific overrides.
Provide bit-level read and write helpers for fixed-width and non-symmetric integer encodings.

summary: Encodes and decodes the WebRTC playout delay RTP header extension. The package owns extension identifiers, delay bounds, error sentinels, and conversion between millisecond delay values and the packed 12-bit wire format.
responsibilities: Define the playout delay RTP header extension URI and bounds.
Clamp requested playout delay values to the representable maximum.
Marshal min and max delay values into the three-byte RTP header extension payload.
Unmarshal min and max delay values from packed RTP header extension bytes.

summary: Maintains RTP sender and receiver statistics for LiveKit SFU media paths. The package owns packet counters, loss and duplicate accounting, jitter and RTT tracking, RTCP sender and receiver report conversion, snapshot deltas, protobuf export, and lightweight variants used when full timing state is unnecessary.
responsibilities: Track full and lightweight RTP sender and receiver packet statistics.
Maintain snapshots and delta windows for reporting intervals.
Process RTCP sender reports and reception reports for RTT, jitter, loss, propagation delay, and clock skew state.
Convert statistics into log objects, protobuf RTPStats, RTCP reports, and aggregate or RTX-reconciled results.

summary: Allocates subscriber video streams across tracked downtracks based on bandwidth estimates, RTCP feedback, congestion state, track priority, and layer availability. It serializes allocation events, manages probing, and emits stream state updates when tracks become active or bandwidth-paused.
responsibilities: Track video downtracks, priority, stream state, max subscribed layer, and allocation dirtiness.
Consume REMB, transport-wide feedback, BWE congestion transitions, pacer probe events, and downtrack layer changes.
Allocate one track or all tracks under stable, deficient, paused, and congestion conditions.
Manage padding or media probing to discover extra capacity.
Notify callers about active and paused stream state changes.

summary: Tracks whether RTP streams and layers are active, stopped, paused, and bitrate-available. The package provides generic stream tracker orchestration plus packet-count, frame-rate, and dependency-descriptor based tracker implementations.
responsibilities: Define stream status and status-change contracts.
Track stream activity using packet samples, frame markers, or dependency descriptors.
Report per-temporal-layer bitrate and bitrate availability changes.
Coordinate pause, reset, generation, worker, and callback behavior.
Provide layered dependency-descriptor wrappers for spatial layer status and bitrate.

summary: Provides SFU utility helpers for debouncing callbacks, codec and RTP packet validation, generic range value tracking, and spreading down track writes across subscribers. The package owns reusable support code used by SFU media paths without depending on other packages in this repository.
responsibilities: Debounce callback execution with resettable timers.
Find codec and RTP header extension matches and validate RTP packets.
Track values across excluded RTP sequence or timestamp ranges.
Store, snapshot, and broadcast over down tracks with concurrency-safe access.

summary: Selects which spatial and temporal video layers should be forwarded for simulcast, VP9 SVC, and dependency-descriptor based streams. The package tracks target, current, maximum, and maximum-seen layers, rewrites dependency descriptor state when needed, and caches frame forwarding decisions for decodability.
responsibilities: Define the video layer selector result and selector contract.
Maintain common layer selection state shared by selector implementations.
Select simulcast, VP9, and dependency-descriptor based video layers.
Track frame chain integrity and decode target validity.
Cache forwarded, dropped, missing, and unknown frame decisions for out-of-order and NACK handling.

summary: Provides temporal layer selection helpers for video forwarding. This generated index covers the selector interface and VP8 temporal layer selector implementation, with `null.go` intentionally excluded by request.
responsibilities: Define the temporal layer selector contract.
Select current and next temporal layers from packet metadata.
Use VP8 payload descriptor information to avoid unsafe temporal layer switches.
Coordinate temporal layer upswitch and downswitch decisions for forwarded packets.

summary: The telemetry package coordinates LiveKit telemetry collection, analytics delivery, webhook notifications, participant stats aggregation, and network connection metrics. It exposes the main telemetry service contract, no-op implementations, event emission helpers, stats workers, and wrappers that record Prometheus counters for connections and RTP stats.
responsibilities: Define the TelemetryService and AnalyticsService contracts used by room, participant, track, ingress, egress, report, API, webhook, and stats flows.
Queue webhook notifications and analytics events through a serialized operation queue.
Track participant stats workers and periodically flush coalesced analytics stats.
Record Prometheus metrics for participants, tracks, RTP stats, connections, packets, bytes, and signal-adjacent telemetry.
Provide no-op telemetry and analytics services for disabled telemetry paths.
Wrap network listeners, stream connections, packet connections, and TURN relay allocation with telemetry counters.

summary: Defines Prometheus metrics and recording helpers for LiveKit node, packet, room, quality, data packet, debug, and platform node telemetry. The package initializes metric collectors with node labels and exposes functions that update counters, gauges, histograms, and protobuf node statistics.
responsibilities: Initialize Prometheus collectors for node, packet, room, quality, data packet, and debug telemetry.
Record SFU packet, RTCP, participant, room, track, session, and forwarding metrics.
Build node statistics and rate snapshots from counters and platform resource measurements.
Provide platform-specific helpers for CPU, load average, and traffic control packet statistics.

summary: Provides shared utility helpers for context values, logging component labels, math and slice helpers, protocol cloning, change notifications, incremental dispatch, ICE config caching, and asynchronous operation queues. The package owns reusable support code used across the server without depending on other packages in this repository.
responsibilities: Store and retrieve request-scoped attempt and logger values from contexts.
Provide generic math, slice, and protocol-copy helpers.
Manage observers, incremental item dispatch, TTL-based ICE config caching, and asynchronous operation queues.
Define logging component constants shared by other packages.
